22.title: Art of iron man
22.author: John Rhett Thomas
22.description: This official Marvel art book takes readers behind the scenes of the Iron Man movie, showcasing the evolution of Tony Stark’s armor, concept artwork, storyboards, and visual effects designs used to bring the character to life on screen.

19.title: Cinematic Storytelling
19.author: Thomas Robotham
19.description: This book offers a comprehensive guide to cinematic coverage and visual storytelling. It focuses on how key frames and shot patterns support the story’s meaning, featuring numerous film examples, storyboard breakdowns, camera diagrams, and practical exercises for directors and cinematographers.

15.title: The Hobbit
15.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
15.description: A classic fantasy novel that follows the journey of Bilbo Baggins, a reluctant hobbit who embarks on an unexpected adventure with a group of dwarves to reclaim their homeland from the dragon Smaug. Along the way, Bilbo encounters trolls, elves, goblins, and discovers a mysterious ring that will shape the fate of Middle-earth.

14.title: Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows
14.author: J.K. Rowling
14.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows.png
14.description: The seventh and final book in the Harry Potter series follows Harry, Ron, and Hermione as they embark on a dangerous mission to find and destroy Voldemort’s Horcruxes. As the wizarding world falls into darkness, the trio faces perilous challenges, uncover deep secrets, and fight in the ultimate battle between good and evil at Hogwarts.

18.title: The Art of Pixar
18.author: Amid Amidi
18.description: This art book celebrates 25 years of Pixar Animation Studios, featuring hundreds of pieces of concept art, storyboards, color scripts, and character designs from all of Pixar’s films up to Cars 2. It offers a behind-the-scenes look at the studio’s creative process and artistic evolution.

7.title: The Catcher in the Rye
7.author: J.D. Salinger
7.description: This classic coming-of-age novel follows Holden Caulfield, a disenchanted teenager who recounts a few days after being expelled from prep school. Wandering through New York City, Holden struggles with themes of alienation, innocence, and the challenges of growing up in a world he sees as “phony.”

9.title: Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets
9.author: J.K. Rowling
9.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets.png
9.description: The second book in the Harry Potter series follows Harry’s return to Hogwarts, where mysterious attacks turn students to stone and strange messages appear on the walls. As fear spreads through the school, Harry, Ron, and Hermione uncover the legend of the Chamber of Secrets and face the monster lurking within.

11.title: Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire
11.author: Thomas Robotham
11.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire.webp
11.description: The fourth book in the Harry Potter series centers on the Triwizard Tournament, a magical competition between three wizarding schools. Harry is unexpectedly chosen as a fourth contestant and faces a series of dangerous tasks. As the challenges unfold, dark forces rise again, marking the return of Lord Voldemort and changing Harry’s world forever.

13.title: Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince
13.author: J.K. Rowling
13.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Half-Blood Prince.png
13.description: The sixth installment in the Harry Potter series delves into Voldemort’s past and the dark secrets that shaped him. With Dumbledore’s guidance, Harry explores the mystery of the Horcruxes—objects containing pieces of Voldemort’s soul. Meanwhile, tensions rise at Hogwarts, and an old book belonging to the “Half-Blood Prince” leads Harry down unexpected paths.

21.title: The Story of Film
21.author: Mark Cousins
21.description: This comprehensive book traces the history of world cinema from its silent beginnings to the digital age. Divided into three main eras — silent (1885–1928), sound (1928–1990), and digital (1990–present) — it explores how filmmakers and cinematic movements across the globe have influenced each other. Cousins connects Hollywood classics, European art films, Asian innovations, and African storytelling, explaining key techniques such as lighting, framing, and editing in clear, accessible language.

17.title: Dune
17.author: Frank Herbert
17.description: A science fiction masterpiece set on the desert planet Arrakis, Dune follows Paul Atreides, heir to a noble family entrusted with the planet’s valuable spice trade. As political betrayal and rebellion erupt, Paul must embrace his destiny as the prophesied leader who will change the fate of humanity. The novel explores themes of power, religion, ecology, and survival, and is widely regarded as one of the greatest sci-fi novels ever written.

16.title: The Lord of the Rings
16.author: J.R.R. Tolkien
16.description: An epic high-fantasy saga set in the richly imagined world of Middle-earth. The story follows Frodo Baggins, a humble hobbit, who embarks on a perilous quest to destroy the One Ring—an artifact of immense power created by the dark lord Sauron. Alongside his loyal companions, Frodo faces trials of courage, friendship, and sacrifice in a battle between good and evil that defines the fate of the world.

10.title: Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban
10.author: J.K. Rowling
10.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Prisoner of Azkaban.jpeg
10.description: The third book in the Harry Potter series follows Harry’s third year at Hogwarts, where news breaks that the dangerous prisoner Sirius Black has escaped from Azkaban and is supposedly hunting Harry. As mysterious events unfold, Harry learns shocking truths about his parents, his past, and the man he thought was his enemy.

12.title: Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix
12.author: J.K. Rowling
12.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Order of the Phoenix.png
12.description: The fifth book in the Harry Potter series sees Harry returning to Hogwarts amid growing denial of Voldemort’s return. As the Ministry of Magic interferes with the school through the cruel Dolores Umbridge, Harry forms “Dumbledore’s Army” to teach his friends defensive spells. The story explores themes of rebellion, leadership, and loss as Harry faces visions connected to Voldemort and the prophecy that binds their fates.

1.title: Pride and Prejudice
1.author: Jane Austen
1.description: This classic romantic novel follows Elizabeth Bennet, a witty and independent young woman, as she navigates issues of love, reputation, and social class in early 19th-century England. Her initial prejudice toward the proud Mr. Darcy gradually transforms into understanding and love, revealing Austen’s timeless commentary on manners, marriage, and morality.

6.title: Little Women
6.author: Louisa May Alcott
6.description: A beloved coming-of-age novel that follows the four March sisters—Meg, Jo, Beth, and Amy—as they grow up during the American Civil War. Through their joys, struggles, and dreams, the story explores themes of family, love, ambition, and independence. Jo March’s spirited pursuit of writing and self-discovery has made her one of literature’s most iconic heroines.

3.title: The Great Gatsby
3.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
3.description: Set in the Jazz Age of 1920s America, this classic novel tells the story of the mysterious millionaire Jay Gatsby and his obsessive love for Daisy Buchanan. Narrated by Nick Carraway, it explores themes of wealth, illusion, desire, and the American Dream—revealing the emptiness beneath the glittering surface of high society.

23.title: The Art of Captain America
23.author: Alan Cowsill
23.description: A comprehensive illustrated look at the eight-decade history of Captain America — from his creation in 1940, through his various identities (Steve Rogers, Sam Wilson) and inspired spin-offs (such as Captain Carter and Iron Patriot). This volume features exclusive interviews with artists and creators, full-color panels, cover art, behind-the-scenes illustrations, and explores how the character has evolved and remained culturally relevant over time.

2.title: To kill a mocking bird
2.author: Harper Lee
2.description: Set in the racially divided American South during the 1930s, this Pulitzer Prize–winning novel follows young Scout Finch as she witnesses her father, Atticus Finch, defend a Black man falsely accused of a grave crime. Through Scout’s innocent eyes, the story explores themes of justice, prejudice, empathy, and moral growth — making it one of the most influential works in modern American literature.

5.title: the Kite runner
5.author: Khaled Hosseini
5.description: This powerful debut novel tells the story of Amir, a boy from Kabul, and his complicated friendship with Hassan, the son of his father’s servant. Spanning from Afghanistan’s peaceful pre-war days to its turbulent modern era, the story explores guilt, redemption, and the enduring power of friendship. The Kite Runner captures the emotional cost of betrayal and the possibility of forgiveness in a changing world.

4.title: THE ALCHEMIST
4.author: Paulo Coelho
4.description: This internationally acclaimed novel follows Santiago, a young Andalusian shepherd, on his journey to the Egyptian desert in search of a hidden treasure. Along the way, he meets mysterious guides who help him discover the deeper meaning of his quest — that true treasure lies in following one’s dreams and listening to one’s heart. The Alchemist is a timeless tale about destiny, faith, and self-discovery.

8.title: Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone
8.author: J.K. Rowling
8.cover: image/Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone.png
8.description: The first book in the beloved Harry Potter series introduces readers to Harry Potter, an orphan who discovers he is a wizard on his eleventh birthday. Attending Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry, he makes new friends, learns about magic, and uncovers the mystery of the Sorcerer’s Stone — all while facing the dark wizard Lord Voldemort for the first time.

24.title: Painting with Light
24.author: John Alton
24.description: This is a foundational work on cinematography by one of Hollywood’s most influential cinematographers. Alton explains in accessible language how lighting, camera work, choice of locations, and visual design combine to set mood and narrative in film.

25.title: Film as Art
25.author: Rudolf Arnheim
25.description: This book is a foundational work of film theory and aesthetics. Arnheim argues that film can be a true art form by emphasizing its unique medium-specific qualities—its visual nature, editing, framing, lighting, the absence of other senses, etc.—rather than by trying to imitate reality or other arts.

26.title: How to Read a Film
26.author: James Monaco
26.description: This influential work presents film (and media more broadly) as an art form, a technology, a language, a history, and a theoretical field. Monaco explores how films create meaning, their relation to other narrative media such as novels, painting, television, and music, and covers major developments in technology (image, sound), film language (signs, syntax), the history and theory of film, the emergence of multimedia and digital contexts.
